2. Type
The Forest Preserve Land is basically a Natural Refuge and Recreation Area.
3. Available Activities
Picnics, Social Gatherings, Hiking and related outdoor pastimes.
4. Facilities Existing and Planned
Existing: open areas for picnicing and wooded areas for hiking with a parking lot area and a foot bridge over Thorn Creek.
Planned: At the present time no additional facilities
are planned.
5. Usage
Current usage is primarily local. The facility is open and available to the general public on a year round basis.
Patronage
The facility is patronized by residents in the immediate area as well as by the population in surrounding areas of Southern Cook County.
7. Relationship to other Similarly Used Land in the Area
Woodrow Wilson Woods is a part of the Thorn Creek Division of the Cook County Forest Preserve District. A general location and diagram of this Division is shown in Exhibit D &
8. Access
Vehicle access to the Forest Preserve is from Lincoln Highway in the area of the study with a newly constructed parking lot. There are also other pedestrian entrances to this land on the north, east, and west sides.
9. Ownership
The Cook County Forest Preserve District is sole owner of this forest preserve property .
10. Deed Restrictions and Reversionary Clauses
The easement for removal of wing walls and reconstruction of the entrance driveway for the Forest Preserve District is temporary and includes approximately 0.17 acres of land which must be returned to its original condition when the highway and bridge improvement are completed.
